kernel_crng_source_audit.getrandom: random-6.12.112.c 1378-1404 validates GRND flags, waits/checks readiness, copies through get_random_bytes_user. Keep this syscall/device behavior for Linux fidelity.
kernel_crng_source_audit.extraction: random-6.12.112.c 662-709 combines prior input_pool with RDSEED, RDRAND or random_get_entropy on every extraction. Merely writing a world seed into the pool leaves prior/native inputs.
kernel_crng_source_audit.reseed: random-6.12.112.c 224-290 schedules delayed reseed work with kernel time; updates base key, generation and vDSO generation.
kernel_crng_source_audit.buffered_state: base_crng, per-CPU crngs and get_random_u32/u64 batches are distinct mutable state. Snapshot reseeding must invalidate/reset all relevant buffered state, readiness, pending work and vDSO userspace state, not just feed /dev/urandom.
kernel_crng_source_audit.pool_ioctl: RNDCLEARPOOL/RNDZAPENTCNT are no-ops at 1528-1533; RNDRESEEDCRNG at 1534-1543 extracts existing pool/native inputs.
kernel_crng_source_audit.guarded_cpu_rng: archrandom-6.12.112.h 49-56 guards generic CPU RNG calls with static_cpu_has; low-level rdrand_long/rdseed_long are unconditional. Hiding CPUID only protects audited callers using the guards.
kernel_crng_source_audit.earlier_patch_limit: early-rng-scope.patch controls only random_init_early through random_init, preserves untouched prior pool, then restores native extraction. Its scoped results do not establish a runtime getrandom profile.
kernel_crng_source_audit.proposed_control_boundary_unimplemented: A world-owned entropy extractor installed before earliest CRNG extraction, deterministic declared readiness and reseed policy, world-controlled clock/interrupt/device influences, no native hwrng/virtio-rng/bootloader input. Preserve Linux ChaCha fast key erasure and syscall/device semantics. Disable vDSO getrandom initially or include its state and paths in conformance. Full CRNG/input-pool state must remain controlled for O1.
kernel_crng_source_audit.must_execute_next: Actual Linux getrandom, /dev/urandom and kernel get_random_* repeated fresh boots plus periodic/forced reseed; perturb native CPU RNG/timing and omit a control as a sensitive negative. No Linux RNG acceptance is claimed here.

initial_workload_envelope: Trusted Redis, etcd, Postgres or Rust service builds are candidates only when their kernel and all libraries route active entropy paths through admitted CRNG interfaces. Application language is not evidence of RNG admission. Fork/exec and dynamic linking need executable-artifact ownership and CRNG conformance, even with no JIT.
scope_limit: No broad Linux/O1/O2, cold-boot entropy closure, full instruction admission or complete state witness accepted.
